statement: Sumitomo Chemical has started mass production and sales of 4-inch indium phosphide epitaxial wafers at its Ibaraki Works, targeting around 10 billion yen of sales from the line by the mid-2030s.
why: Indium phosphide wafers are the base material for the optical parts that move data between AI racks, so a new qualified supplier widens a narrow upstream chokepoint.

impact.mechanism: Added mass-production capacity for optical wafer substrates increases the supply of components needed for high-speed data-center interconnect.

evidence.source: Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd. (official news release)
evidence.excerpt: The company has established mass production of '4-inch indium phosphide (InP) epitaxial wafers' at its Ibaraki Works in Hitachi, Ibaraki Prefecture, and has begun selling the new products.

confidence.basis: Company news release classified as secondary in this fetch; the sales target is a long-dated company goal, not a committed volume.
